questions.question: Which of the following is a common type of seed used in school laboratories that can easily germinate on wet cotton wool under the right conditions?
options: Cress seeds
Acorn seeds
Coconut seeds
Sunflower seeds

questions.question: How do flowering plants primarily reproduce?
options: Asexually through budding
Sexually, involving male and female sex cells
Solely by producing identical clones from roots
Through binary fission

questions.question: Which of the following statements about flowers is correct?
options: They contain only female reproductive structures.
They contain only male reproductive structures.
They contain both male and female sex organs and gametes.
They lack sex organs and reproduce using spores.

questions.question: What is the name of the female gamete in a flowering plant?
options: Pollen grain
Egg cell (ovum)
Anther
Filament

questions.question: What do pollen grains carry in flowering plants?
options: Female gametes
Male gametes
Nutrients for the growing fruit
Seeds to be dispersed

questions.question: What are the three main components that make up a seed, and where is the seed formed?
options: Embryo, food store, and a tough outer coat; formed in the ovary
Pollen, nectar, and a shell; formed in the anther
Root, stem, and leaf; formed in the stigma
Spore, capsule, and stalk; formed in the petal

questions.question: What biological structure does a fruit develop from?
options: The ripened pollen tube
The mature and ripened ovary of a seed-producing plant
The swollen petals of the flower after pollination
The sepals that have fused together

questions.question: What is the primary role of a pollinator in plant reproduction?
options: To consume the seeds of the plant so they can be digested
To transfer pollen from one flower to another, enabling sexual reproduction
To release carbon dioxide near the leaves to increase photosynthesis
To protect the flower buds from wind damage

questions.question: Which group of animals makes up the majority of pollinators, and which specific group within them is the largest?
options: Birds, with hummingbirds being the largest group
Mammals, with bats being the largest group
Insects, with bees being the largest group
Reptiles, with lizards being the largest group

questions.question: What does the term "food security" mean for a population?
options: Having advanced locking systems on agricultural warehouses
Ensuring all food produced is organic and GMO-free
Having enough affordable and nutritious food in an area or country
Having a backup supply of canned food for a minimum of ten years

questions.question: What is pollination?
options: The fusion of male and female nuclei in the ovary
The transfer of pollen from the male anther to the female stigma
The release of seeds from a manual fruit into the wind
The process of water moving up the stem to the flower

questions.question: What is a major advantage of cross-pollination compared to self-pollination?
options: It requires fewer pollinators to be present.
It increases genetic variation in a species.
It guarantees that offspring will be exact clones of the parent.
It takes less time to complete fertilisation.

questions.question: In plant reproduction, what occurs during the process of fertilisation?
options: The pollen grain lands on the sticky surface of the stigma.
The fusion of the nuclei from the male and the female gametes.
The dispersal of seeds away from the parent plant by the wind.
The splitting open of the anther to release pollen.

questions.question: When presenting experimental data, how should you choose between drawing a line graph and a bar chart?
options: Use a line graph for categoric independent variables and a bar chart for continuous ones.
Use a line graph for continuous independent variables and a bar chart for categoric ones.
Use a line graph when there are more than ten results and a bar chart for fewer than ten.
Use a line graph for temperature changes and a bar chart for time measurements.

questions.question: Why do plants disperse their seeds using different mechanisms?
options: To increase the chance of seed survival by reducing competition.
To ensure all seeds land in the exact same spot.
To allow the seeds to undergo self-pollination before they grow.
To prevent the parent plant from producing any more flowers.

questions.question: How is a seed adapted for wind dispersal?
options: It is heavy with a small surface area to sink quickly.
It is covered in sharp hooks to cling to passing animals.
It is light with a large surface area to catch the breeze.
It is surrounded by a tasty, fleshy fruit to attract birds.

questions.question: Why is it important to repeat measurements for each value when investigating seed dispersal?
options: To change the independent variable halfway through the experiment.
To identify anomalous results and calculate a mean.
To guarantee that every single trial gives the exact same measurement.
To increase the total time the investigation takes.
